context: A civics lecture on how the cabinet works
purpose: Explain government; teach 総理/国務大臣/副/局長/裁判所/義務/差別/設立

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 今日は内閣の仕組みを学びます。
lines.en: Today we learn how the cabinet works.
lines.style: organized teacher opening the lesson, each word carrying genuine natural feeling

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 総理大臣が中心なんですよね。
lines.en: The prime minister is at the center, right?
lines.style: engaged student confirming the basics, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ええ、各省庁に国務大臣がいます。
lines.en: Yes, each ministry has a minister of state.
lines.style: teacher building out the structure, tone holding steady through the whole line

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 副大臣や局長は、どんな役割ですか？
lines.en: What roles do deputy ministers and bureau directors play?
lines.style: curious teen drilling into detail, delivery emotionally grounded and unforced

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 大臣を支え、実務を取り仕切ります。
lines.en: They support the minister and run the operations.
lines.style: teacher clarifying the hierarchy, spoken with a recognizable personal cadence

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 法律を作るのは国会、裁くのは裁判所ですね。
lines.en: The Diet makes laws; courts judge, right?
lines.style: student mapping the separation of powers

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: その通り。国民には納税の義務もあります。
lines.en: Exactly. Citizens also have the duty to pay taxes.
lines.style: teacher connecting to civic duty, each word carrying genuine natural feeling

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 差別をなくす法律も、ここで作られるんですね。
lines.en: Laws to end discrimination are made here too.
lines.style: teen connecting it to real issues

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ええ、新しい委員会の設立も検討されています。
lines.en: Yes, founding a new committee is under consideration.
lines.style: teacher adding a current example, voice clear and distinctly their own
